entries.subject: Temperature at 15 um from the same ten JWST MIRI visits
entries.finding: The lens, as a labelled model. c's dayside is measured and its day-night pattern is not: its eclipse depth in the joint fit is 318 to 389 ppm (Bell's shape, a symmetric sinusoid, a free one), a 15 um brightness temperature of 353 to 379 K; its four eclipse visits alone give 331 to 463 ppm. The phase curve does not constrain c (freed, the sinusoid runs to its bound; held symmetric, its amplitude fits to zero), so no map is fitted. The lens draws a bare rock (T cos(z)^(1/4), nothing at night; Cowan & Agol 2011, eq. 3), the model b's light curve supports, set to show the middle of the depth range: 407 K under the star, 392 to 421 K across it, below the 480 K of a black rock. A dark night is the model's assumption. A phase curve that constrains c's day-night contrast, or a published map of c, would replace the model with a fit.
